draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Sindhudurg Fort! Chhatrapati Shivaji commissioned this sea fort on Kurte island off Malvan, and it was built between 1664 and 1667. Today it's a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India.
draft.hungryLine: Malvan is famous for seafood, so go straight for fresh fried fish.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Catch the ferry out to Sindhudurg Fort, then come back for the rock garden near the fort. Tarkarli beach is 6 km south of Malvan.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: The rock garden near Sindhudurg Fort is the spot for sunset, sitting right on the rocks.
moodReplies.surprise-me: At Tarkarli, just down the coast, the water is so clear that on a good day you can see the sea bed 20 ft down.

tips.title: Go out early.
tips.body: Ferries to the fort have run from 8 in the morning with the last boat at 5PM, so check today's timings and don't miss the boat back.

tips.title: Try snorkelling.
tips.body: The MTDC quarters offer snorkelling near Sindhudurg.

story.title: A fort in the sea
story.body: Shivaji began building this ocean fort on Kurte island in 1664, to the glory of the Maratha Empire. Work finished in 1667.

story.title: Malvan's landmark
story.body: Malvan grew as a fishing port town of about 19,000 people, but it's still best known for this fort just offshore.

story.title: Protected monument
story.body: Sindhudurg Fort is now protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Boats carry visitors across from Malvan through the day.
